title: Book Two · Chapter 34: The Brass Handle
story:
The button shop has three small drawers of blue buttons.

On Saturday, Mum puts her old button on the counter. Ronan stands beside her. He likes the brightest blue ones, but their centres are too large.

Mum chooses four smaller buttons. The shopkeeper wraps them in paper. Ronan carries the little packet while they walk to Mr Sun's counter.

Dad is speaking to an older woman. A brown wooden box is open between them. Its small drawer has a brass handle.

“I remember it,” Dad says.

“So do I,” the woman says. “I still need two hands for this drawer.”

She pulls the handle. The drawer moves a little and stops. Dad puts one hand against the side of the box and helps her.

Ronan stays beside Mum. He wants to say Dad can fix it. Mum touches his shoulder before he speaks.

Dad lifts the drawer out. There are old pencil marks underneath.

“I put this piece in,” he says. “At the old shop.”

“It was better for a while.”

“Yes.”

He looks along the side. Mr Sun comes over and checks the edge with him. Then Dad puts the drawer on the cloth.

“May I look at it more carefully? I cannot tell you the full problem yet.”

“I can leave it,” the woman says. “But please do not make another quick promise.”

Dad nods.

Mr Sun writes her name on a work card. She tells him the box holds small pieces of jewellery. She has left those at home.

They agree to talk again in two weeks, on Saturday. The woman will come to the counter. There is no new price on the card yet.

After she leaves, Dad sits for a moment. Mum puts the buttons in her own bag.

“Can we go home?” Ronan asks.

“Soon. I need to finish here first.”

Mr Sun lets Dad take the box home for the weekend. Dad must bring it back on Monday. The work card stays with Mr Sun.

Ronan waits while Dad puts the drawer back. Dad wraps the box in an old cloth and carries it himself.

On the road, Ronan looks at the brass handle through a gap in the cloth.

“Did she buy that box from you?”

“No. She brought it for a repair.”

“And you fixed it?”

“I changed a piece. I did the work too quickly. The wood was not ready. Later, the drawer began to stick again.”

“Did you know about the wood?”

“I needed more time. I knew that. I still told her it was ready.”

They walk past the fruit shop. Dad stops to let a cart pass.

“Will you fix it now?”

“I will look at it first.”

At home, Dad puts the box on his work cloth. Ronan places his hands behind his back.

Dad turns the box towards the light. The old pencil lines are still underneath. He looks at them for a long time before he reaches for a tool.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

brass＝黄铜；drawer＝抽屉；jewellery＝首饰；stick＝卡住、不好移动。

## 理解问题

1. 旧顾客为什么提醒Dad不要再很快作出承诺？
2. 木盒周末和周一分别应该在哪里？

## 读句子

Dad / wraps the box / in an old cloth.＝Dad／把盒子包起来／用一块旧布。
